title: Subquery in FROM Clause (Derived Table / Inline View)
description: Find all **product categories that contain more products than the average number of products per category**. Use a subquery in the FROM clause as a derived table to first compute counts, then filter against the average.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE products (product_id INT, name VARCHAR(100), category VARCHAR(50), price DECIMAL(10,2)); INSERT INTO products VALUES (1,'Widget A','Electronics',29.99),(2,'Widget B','Electronics',49.99),(3,'Widget C','Electronics',19.99),(4,'Widget D','Electronics',99.99),(5,'Gadget A','Toys',14.99),(6,'Gadget B','Toys',24.99),(7,'Tool A','Hardware',39.99),(8,'Tool B','Hardware',59.99),(9,'Tool C','Hardware',79.99),(10,'Book A','Books',12.99),(11,'Shirt A','Clothing',34.99),(12,'Pants A','Clothing',54.99);
solution_sql: SELECT category, product_count FROM (SELECT category, COUNT(*) AS product_count FROM products GROUP BY category) cat_counts WHERE product_count > (SELECT AVG(product_count) FROM (SELECT COUNT(*) AS product_count FROM products GROUP BY category) sub) ORDER BY product_count DESC

test_cases.description: 5 categories: Electronics(4), Hardware(3), Toys(2), Clothing(2), Books(1). Average=2.4. Electronics and Hardware exceed the average.

hints: Place a GROUP BY subquery in the FROM clause to pre-compute counts per category — this derived table can then be referenced in the outer WHERE clause.
The average to compare against must itself come from a subquery since you cannot use aggregate functions in a WHERE clause.
explanation: The derived table in FROM materializes category counts: Electronics=4, Hardware=3, Toys=2, Clothing=2, Books=1 — average=12/5=2.4. The outer WHERE filters rows where product_count > 2.4, yielding Electronics(4) and Hardware(3). A second subquery computes the AVG because WHERE cannot directly reference aggregates.
